causalAssessment.physicalRegime: Still tight/strong. Copper had moved above USD13,000/t around the checkpoint and mine/supply concerns had not disappeared.
causalAssessment.companyRealizedEconomics: No new company financial report was available by the checkpoint that could prove an earnings step-up beyond the Q1-Q3 2025 base used at selection.
causalAssessment.incrementalSurprise: Closing. The copper shortage/AI-grid narrative had moved from a December underwritten thesis into a widely recognized record-price regime.
causalAssessment.expectationGap: Likely materially compressed. Record copper prices and broad market attention reduce the margin for additional surprise even if the physical regime persists.

evidence.summary: Reuters Breakingviews noted copper above USD13,000/t despite muted manufacturing and framed the move as a bottleneck increasingly driven by tariff stockpiling and AI/grid demand.
Bloomberg reported that Chinese industrial buyers were sharply reducing purchases after copper reached record prices, creating direct evidence of demand-destruction risk.
A Reuters-syndicated report said SHFE copper had recently hit a record and LME copper remained around USD13,156/t, with optimism on Chinese demand policy and supply factors still supporting prices.

checkpointRulesApplied.currentSurprise: At selection, the surprise was that tight supply plus AI/grid demand could sustain copper economics despite an already-large stock move.
closureIndicatorsTriggered: copper price itself moved into a new record regime
physical Chinese industrial demand showed signs of retreat at record prices
the shortage/AI-grid narrative became broadly recognized
no new company-specific earnings disclosure by checkpoint proved that the profit bridge had expanded enough to offset expectation saturation

rationale: Exit is based on causal/expectation re-underwriting, not on the checkpoint return. The physical copper regime remained strong, but the incremental surprise gap had compressed sharply and demand-destruction evidence appeared. V3.3 therefore closes the historical trade at the first checkpoint and forbids opening later selected-stock price segments.
